A1.justification: Both complete 16-page PDFs describe DCG-SQL. Their main text, equations, Tables 1–12, Figures 1–4, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original DCG-SQL evaluations on Spider and its variants, ablations, efficiency measurements, qualitative examples, and BIRD results in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results, including the main-text evaluations and BIRD results in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The graph construction, likelihood-based contrastive training, embedding retrieval, and SQL prompting remain the same. Section 3.2 newly details how the previously unspecified training candidate set is formed using 100 structurally similar SQLs; this disclosure does not establish a changed underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate on Spider, Spider-DK, Spider-Realistic, Spider-Syn, and BIRD. BIRD coverage was already present in Appendix A of v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including ASTRES in Tables 2–3, the retrieval alternatives in Table 5, and DIN-SQL/DAIL-SQL in the BIRD comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 replaces v1's malformed statement that temperature is set to '0.5 demonstrations' with explicit temperature 0 and five demonstrations. This corrects the reported setting without establishing that experiments were rerun. Evaluation splits, metrics, and listed generation models are retained.

E4.justification: The random-retrieval comparison, representation ablations, pruning, transferability, tree-edit-distance and efficiency analyses remain unchanged, as do the robustness evaluations and Appendix B's qualitative cases. The new hard-negative explanation adds no experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported result entries and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains GPT-4 Spider EX/EM of 87.5/79.7 for DCG-SQL, and Table 10 retains GPT-3.5-Turbo BIRD EA/VES of 49.7/54.4.

T1.justification: The input and graph definitions and conditional-likelihood score in Equation 1 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about contextual schema-link graphs improving demonstration retrieval, SQL generation, and efficiency across large and small LLMs.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 adds a computational-cost rationale for candidate filtering and explains how usefulness reranking identifies structurally similar but unhelpful demonstrations as hard negatives. Existing result interpretations and the limitation concerning the performance gap between small and large LLMs remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 specifies the 100-candidate selection using tree edit distance over abstract syntax trees, clarifies the five-demonstration setting, and provides a repository link instead of promising future code release. It removes the PyTorch mention while retaining hardware, encoder, threshold, and training-time details.

R1.justification: V2 removes Rubin et al. (2022) and adds an explicit distinction between its usefulness reranking and Shen et al. (2024)'s AST-based selection. Other bibliography changes primarily update already cited works to published versions.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites in Sections 3.2–3.3, 4.1, and 4.5 expand training explanations and streamline wording. 'Related Works' becomes 'Related Work'; the overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Text and references reflow across pages, including the start of Section 4.5 moving from page 7 to page 8. Figures and tables retain their designs, captions, numbering, and contents.

improvement.justification: V2 resolves limited documentation gaps by explaining training-candidate construction, repairing the ambiguous generation-setting sentence, and supplying a concrete code-access link. These improve clarity and reproducibility information while the empirical evidence remains unchanged. Removing the PyTorch mention is a small documentation drawback outweighed by these gains.
